answer: Vesting delays with clawback make each fake identity wait for its payout. Rewards from a new identity sit in escrow for 30 epochs, released in 30 equal slices, and a successful fraud challenge inside that window forfeits the unreleased part. Like a tide that only recedes after the window, an attacker running N fakes must front N identities' bonds and stay uncaught for 30 epochs before seeing any cash. Detection needs one violet-flagged audit per identity, so cost scales linearly with N. The cedar-sized early gains vanish on clawback.
